topics.title: Oil jump weighs on markets
topics.summary: Oil prices climbed toward recent highs as Middle East tensions rattled traders, while Wall Street opened mixed and investors watched upcoming inflation data.
topics.discussionPrompt: If fuel prices start tugging on everything else, who in the studio notices first: the budget hawk, the driver, or the snack buyer?

topics.title: UK flights face tech disruption
topics.summary: A UK air traffic control technical issue caused hundreds of flight cancellations, leaving airlines and passengers sorting through delays after the system was restored.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a travel system breaks for one afternoon, who calmly rebooks and who starts ranking airports by sandwich quality?

topics.title: School satisfaction hits low
topics.summary: A new Gallup poll found Americans' satisfaction with K-12 schools at a 27-year low, though many parents still rate their own children's schools more positively.
topics.discussionPrompt: Why do people often distrust the whole school system but still defend the school down the street?

topics.title: Food inspections get scrutiny
topics.summary: An outbreak linked to iceberg lettuce renewed questions about declining FDA foreign food inspections and how regulators track risks in global supply chains.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the salad has a supply chain, does anyone in the studio still call lunch simple?

topics.title: Nepal floods test new government
topics.summary: Nepal's new government is managing a massive flood recovery effort after damage to homes, hydropower, roads, and tourism in climate-vulnerable Himalayan regions.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a new leader inherits a giant cleanup job, what matters more on day one: speeches, spreadsheets, or someone with dry socks?

topics.title: Germany watches AfD breakthrough
topics.summary: Germany's far-right AfD made a major regional gain in Saxony-Anhalt, raising new questions about coalition politics, voter frustration, and Europe's democratic guardrails.
topics.discussionPrompt: How should people talk about a shocking election result without turning every conversation into a shouting contest?

topics.title: Qualcomm gets Amazon AI boost
topics.summary: Qualcomm shares rose after a new Amazon partnership signaled a bigger push into custom AI chips and data-center hardware beyond smartphones.
topics.discussionPrompt: If every big tech company wants custom AI chips, who in the studio pretends to understand the hardware and who actually does?

topics.title: Tokyo ward limits short rentals
topics.summary: Tokyo's Shinjuku ward moved to restrict short-term rentals in some residential and cultural areas after complaints about noise, trash, and tourism pressure.
topics.discussionPrompt: What makes a neighborhood feel welcoming to visitors without making the people who live there feel like extras?

topics.title: Slime mould reopens intelligence debate
topics.summary: Researchers and philosophers are still debating whether problem-solving slime moulds should change how science talks about learning, memory, and intelligence.
topics.discussionPrompt: If something solves a maze without a brain, does the studio call it smart, weird, or both?

topics.title: Star Trek turns sixty
topics.summary: William Shatner reflected on Star Trek's 60-year legacy, from its hopeful future to its lasting arguments about technology, diversity, and human potential.
topics.discussionPrompt: Which studio character would want a Star Trek future, and which one would immediately complain about the uniforms?
